nodes.label: Analysis
nodes.question: How did the researchers determine the period to consider for their data collection related to the hatching date?
nodes.answer: If the hatching date was known, they considered the period from hatching to the following 30 days; if not known, they used the day after deployment plus 30 days.
nodes.paragraph: To make the number of fixes comparable between individuals and years and reduce spatial autocorrelation, we subsampled our tracks, keeping one fix every six hours with a 15-minute time tolerance with the R package amt (Signer et al. 2019 ). In 2022, data related to the breeding period were obtained based on the average length of the lapwing breeding season in Italy (i.e., 25 days of incubation followed by 35 40 days to raise the young; Brichetti and Fracasso 2018 2022 ). If the hatching date was known, we considered the period from hatching to the fol - lowing 30 days; if not, we used the day after deployment plus 30 days. By doing so, we could be sure that our data would fall within the fledging date. Since we had evidence that camera traps were a source of stress for the birds, in 2023 we refrained from using them. Therefore, we assessed each breeding phase through direct field observations and kept only the locations falling between the day after deploy - ment and the fledging date (37 days on average, deemed comparable to the data from 2022).

nodes.label: Management
nodes.question: How did the two approaches in sampling complement each other in data collection?
nodes.answer: The two approaches in sampling, based on sustainability policies and involvement in SPD processes, provided depth and consistency in data collection.

nodes.label: Facts
nodes.question: What year is considered a standard year for catch data in the study?
nodes.answer: The year 2021 is considered a standard year in terms of volumes and species composition.
nodes.paragraph: Each category is associated with a primary gear type, except for the small-scale fleet, which uses multiple gear types. A complete description of the fleets can be found in the sup- plementary material (Supplementary material Table S3). Catch data are assigned to each fleet from official land- ings from the Catalan and Valencian Governments for 2021 for the harbours inside our study area (Castell de la Plana, Pe scola, Benicarl , Vinar S, Burriana, Calafell, Cambrils, Delta Ebre, La R pita, Les Cases d'Alcanar, L'Ametlla de Mar, Tarragona, Torredembarra, and Vilanova i la Geltr ) (Generalitat Valenciana 2021; ICATMAR 2023). 2021 can be considered a standard year in terms of volumes and spe- cies composition following the COVID crisis. The ecologi- cal model has been validated against prior data from the area to ensure its coherence. The link between the food web model and the value chain module was done through the FG landings and the fleet structure provided in the Ecopath model (Table S4 and S5). The basic estimates of the final balanced model, as well as the diet matrix, are presented in the supplementary material (Tables S6 to S7).
